preservation_constraints.requirement: Keep frozen technical baseline `native_godot_project` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

Keep frozen technical baseline `host_godot_boot` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Advance release convergence with two bounded implementation families: restore authored arena spatial integrity and choice-HUD presentation, and expose release-safe native dense-profile timing data for host qualification.

diagnosis.root_cause: Release-convergence evidence shows a major authored-mausoleum camera occlusion defect and a dense-profile native frame-time evidence gap. The phase contract also requires authored upgrade-choice hierarchy and complete input focus behavior, while preserving the intact cemetery package and native technical baselines.

stop_conditions: Preserve the intact authored cemetery package, native streets, OuterDatum, central mausoleum, Warden scene/animation profile, Montserrat typography, and native audio library.

Do not replace, split, hide, duplicate, or surgically modify authored environment geometry; use one authoritative map instance with additive collision, navigation, spawn, objective, and camera-sight bindings.
Do not claim native performance qualification or issue closure; GameLoop Runtime and Tester own recapture, formal verdicts, and phase closure.
Do not add tester-only InputMap actions, debug overlays, unrelated asset replacements, or deferred automatic-attack-audio work.

strategy.rationale: Repair the arena through direct authored-instance, collision, sight-lane, and wrapper/binding restoration rather than another camera-only transform tweak; implement the required choice hierarchy against authoritative build data; and add bounded candidate-side dense timing telemetry so the host can perform native three-cycle qualification.

code: Run targeted static checks/tests for cemetery spatial bindings, collision/navigation alignment, camera visibility handling, upgrade-card normalization/stat filtering/focus, authoritative build mutation, dense-profile sampling, lifecycle reset, and bounded history.
Verify no preserved authored asset/package was replaced or split and no tester-only actions, debug overlays, or unrelated audio changes entered the candidate.
runtime: GameLoop Runtime/Tester recapture release_convergence_survivor_hud_presentation_contract at shipped resolution with spawn, central-landmark route, perimeter, dense gameplay HUD, and upgrade-draft states; exercise keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus/activation and verify the authoritative build snapshot changes exactly once.

GameLoop Runtime/Tester perform same-framing ordinary movement replay around the central building/landmark and perimeter; verify collision, no pass-through, no disappearance/occlusion drift, stable escape-lane visibility, and clean retry behavior.

GameLoop Runtime/Tester recapture release_convergence_dense_run_performance_contract with the software-renderer/native collector at 1920x1080 and 25-40 enemies; require candidate timing samples, renderer eligibility metadata, three-cycle reset provenance, bounded distributions, and no runtime errors or growth across retries.
visual: Compare gameplay and choice-draft captures with the bound Mournlight reference for high-angle framing, cemetery density, warm-versus-cool lighting, readable silhouettes, escape lanes, compact authored HUD, icon-led cards, restrained dividers, and truthful deltas.

Inspect separated world views at spawn, critical landmark route, perimeter, and dense combat; reject visible primitive stand-ins, floating/intersecting props, opaque debug panels, clipped cards, or landmark occlusion.

done_when: The shipped high-angle gameplay camera keeps the player, Warden, nearby threats, and at least one escape lane readable during ordinary movement replay around the central building/landmark.

The central building/landmark has aligned collision, navigation, spawn/objective anchors, and camera clearance; the player cannot pass through it, become hidden behind it, or suffer disappearance/occlusion drift during movement replay.
The arena has larger traversable scale plus coherent external world/external depth, with stable perimeter/boundary visibility and impassable boundary collision.

Upgrade and weapon choices lead with authored silhouettes or icons, use compact stat icons, show truthful current-to-new values for no more than three decision-relevant deltas, omit unchanged/exhaustive rows, never show NEW or LOCKED as a CURRENT value, and use restrained copy.

Keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus, hover, unavailable, pressed, and selected states are visibly distinct without changing card dimensions; a same-loop black-box interaction selects a card and the authoritative build snapshot visibly changes.
First-run guidance, live input glyphs, Montserrat typography, and normal HUD readability remain intact after the spatial/HUD repair.
tasks.instructions: Repair the authored cemetery spatial contract and survivor choice presentation as one player-facing release surface. Use the intact native map as the sole authoritative visual environment; rebase wrapper/OuterDatum, collision layers, navigation, spawn/objective anchors, and camera sight-lane bindings so the central building/landmark and perimeter remain grounded, traversable, and readable. Provide sufficient larger traversable scale and coherent external world/external depth without proxy roads, floor patches, duplicated landmarks, or asset-family expansion. Replace any remaining text-stacked choice rows with authored silhouettes/icons, compact stat deltas, truthful current-to-new values, eligibility filtering, and complete keyboard/mouse/gamepad focus states bound to the authoritative upgrade transaction. Preserve first-run guidance and typography. Tester should be able to black-box replay ordinary movement and choice selection while white-box snapshots verify collision, camera visibility, focus state, and build mutation.
tasks.title: Restore authored arena integrity and choice HUD

done_when: The dense-profile runtime emits bounded candidate-owned native frame-time samples with profile identity, monotonic timestamp, per-frame duration, physics/render timing where available, active-density context, and sample count.

The stream records nonzero samples whenever frames run, supports lifecycle reset and three-cycle provenance, and retains bounded distributions/high-water summaries without unbounded allocations or measurable normal-run presentation overhead.
Instrumentation is gated to the dense profile, release-safe, and absent from shipped UI; no tester-only actions or debug overlays are required for ordinary play.

A host software-renderer or native collector can bind the emitted stream to the exact candidate and independently judge renderer eligibility, frame execution, sample availability, and retry-to-retry growth.
tasks.instructions: Add focused candidate-side instrumentation around the authoritative dense final-wave loop and its lifecycle reset. Emit a bounded machine-readable timing record for each sampled frame (profile/cycle identity, monotonic timestamp, frame duration, physics/render measurements when available, density counters, and sample index), then expose aggregate distributions and reset-isolation receipts for host collection. Keep sampling lightweight and disabled outside the dense qualification path; preserve ordinary gameplay behavior and the native renderer gate. Do not implement a synthetic pass or claim native qualification—the Tester/Runtime will recapture three complete cycles at the required density and resolution.
tasks.title: Expose bounded native dense-profile timing telemetry
